label: Flipkart
terms_note: Flipkart seller account (India, GST); the seller creates a self-access application (id + secret) in the API portal — sharing self-access credentials with third parties gets the account deactivated, so a multi-tenant product must register as a third-party app using the authorization-code flow; tokens 60 d access / 180 d refresh with a '21-day safe window'; HTTPS only; sandbox available; ≤ 10 SKUs per listing request, ≤ 100 shipments per order request; no numeric rate limit published.

discovery.auth: oauth2 (self-access client-credentials with application id/secret from the seller API portal; third-party authorization-code for aggregators; access 60 d, refresh 180 d)
sdks: official code-generation tools for Python and C# (FMSAPI page)

auth: 1. Seller registers an application in the seller API portal → application id + secret (self-access) — or the platform registers a third-party app.
2. Self-access: POST token with Basic(app id:secret) grant_type=client_credentials; third-party: seller authorises → authorization code → token + refresh token.
3. Access token 60 days, refresh 180 days; renew inside the 21-day safe window; check expiry before calls.

endpoints.notes: product_id, price.mrp / selling_price, tax.hsn / tax_code, listing_status, fulfillment_profile, locations[], packages[]; ≤ 10 SKUs

endpoints.purpose: update listing, price only, inventory only

reference.limits: No numeric rate limit on the pages opened; batch caps (10 SKUs, 100 shipments) apply. - Self-access credentials may not be shared with third parties (account deactivation) — multi-tenant use must be a registered third-party app. - HTTPS only; tokens must not be hard-coded. - GST / HSN data mandatory on listings (India).
mcp_sdk: SDK: official code-generation tools for Python and C# (FMSAPI page)

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Seller API access token of your Self Access Application (Seller Dashboard > Manage Profile > Developer Access): obtain it with GET https://api.flipkart.net/oauth-service/oauth/token?grant_type=client_credentials&scope=Seller_Api,Default using HTTP Basic appId:appSecret. It is valid about 60 days; replace it when calls start failing with 401 (the runtime cannot run Flipkart's GET token call itself).

adapter.terms: Flipkart Marketplace Seller APIs (India). Self Access Applications are for the seller's own use only; partners/aggregators must use Third Party Applications.

me.note: No account endpoint; the probe searches one APPROVED pre-dispatch shipment ({shipments[], hasMore, nextPageUrl}) to verify the token.

list_orders.note: Search Shipments POST /v3/shipments/filter/ {filter: {type, states: [status], orderDate: {from: since}}, pagination: {pageSize ≤ 20}}. `status` is REQUIRED and selects the filter type: APPROVED|PACKING_IN_PROGRESS|PACKED|FORM_FAILED|READY_TO_DISPATCH (preDispatch) or SHIPPED|DELIVERED|PICKUP_COMPLETE (postDispatch). One row per SHIPMENT (raw.shipmentId); id/status/total/created_at come from its first order item (INR). Further pages are only reachable through raw.nextPageUrl.

not_offered.create_listing: POST /listings/v3 takes a body keyed by the SKU itself ({"<sku>": {product_id, price, tax, listing_status, shipping_fees, fulfillment_profile, packages, locations}}); object keys built from an argument cannot be expressed, and the vocabulary lacks product_id, HSN/tax and package data.
not_offered.update_listing: POST /listings/v3/update/price uses the same SKU-keyed body ({"<sku>": {product_id, price: {mrp, selling_price, currency}}}), i.e. an object key taken from the argument, which the declarative body cannot build.
not_offered.set_inventory: POST /listings/v3/update/inventory is keyed by SKU ({"<sku>": {product_id, locations: [{id, inventory}]}}) and needs the Flipkart product_id and location id; not expressible with fixed body keys.
not_offered.end_listing: Listing status changes go through POST /listings/v3/update with the same SKU-keyed body (listing_status INACTIVE); not expressible with fixed body keys.
not_offered.mark_shipped: The dispatch calls in the Order Management API reference (POST /v3/shipments/dispatch, POST /v3/shipments/selfShip/dispatch, preceded by /v3/shipments/labels) operate on shipmentIds and the seller's dispatch location rather than an order id plus tracking number; those ids are not vocabulary inputs.

evidence: host api.flipkart.net: DNS ok, TLSv1.2 (GlobalSign nv-sa)
probe: 2/2 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 2/2 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
